summary.text:
An HRA revenue outturn — four pages, appendix included — carrying no treasury figures. No CFR, no loan-book table, no maturity profile, no prudential indicators, no MRP policy, no adviser named. The only treasury-adjacent lines are a £0.087m finance-charge variance and one sentence at paragraph 7 that the higher revenue contribution to capital (£27.734m actual against £23.924m revised) meant no external borrowing was needed for the HRA capital programme in 2025/26. Everything else is repairs, voids, disrepair claims, rent arrears and housing management.

The HRA outturned at a £1.454m deficit against an original £5.352m surplus — a £6.806m movement driven by a £5.322m repairs overspend (responsive repairs, OFS scheduling, damp and mould, voids, electrical and gas), a £3.810m step-up in the revenue contribution to capital, and a £0.953m income shortfall attributed to a week-53 adjustment, partly offset by a £2.323m housing-management underspend and a £1.043m lower bad-debt contribution. Reserves fall from £16.633m to £15.179m, with a further £4.488m draw budgeted for 2026/27 to £10.691m. The arithmetic ties throughout.

No loan-book reconciliation is possible against this paper, and the balance-sheet identity (CFR − external borrowing − OLTL = internal borrowing) cannot be tested — none of the three inputs are printed. For context our file holds 74 PWLB loans totalling £549,079,632 at a weighted 3.7685%, sitting on a c.£120m indicative discount driven by four post-2070 loans at 1.93%–1.96% — but nothing in this paper opens a door to discussing any of that. No email drafted: this is a revenue outturn, not a treasury paper, and there is nothing a treasurer would want to hear us raise off it.

The S151 is Ben Smith, Director of Finance and S151 Officer, named in the paper but with no email address published. The companion Cabinet items on 16 July 2026 — 128904 (General Fund revenue outturn) and 128942 (Capital Outturn and Financing 25/26) — sit on disk but were not read in this pass; 128942 is the item most likely to carry the CFR and external borrowing figure a future draft would need.
